# Which venue moves first? Cross-venue price discovery

*Auto-generated by `scripts/leadlag_note.py` on 2026-08-23 05:56 UTC from `data/history/` (same recorded snapshots as the edge-persistence note).*

## Method

Mids move sparsely at snapshot cadence, so raw return cross-correlation is dominated by zeros. Instead, move-conditional analysis: a *move* is a mid change of at least 0.2500¢ between consecutive co-observed snapshots; for every venue-A move we look ahead up to 10 snapshots for venue B's first move and classify it follow (same direction), oppose, or unanswered. Same-tick moves land in a `simultaneous` bucket — sub-cadence leadership is unobservable and never attributed. Recording gaps split sessions; nothing is measured across a gap. The test statistic is an exact two-sided binomial on follows vs opposes against p = 0.5.

## Reading

- No clear leader at this cadence: follow rates 60% (K→PM) vs 60% (PM→K). Much of the action is in the `simultaneous` bucket — leadership, if any, plays out faster than the snapshot cadence.
- 686 same-tick move pairs vs 801 cross-tick follows: the cadence floor is doing real censoring; the BYOK websocket feed (sub-second) will sharpen this materially.
- Unanswered moves are informative too: a venue whose moves the other never validates is either discovering price alone or drifting on noise/one-sided flow.

## Event study: the 2026-07-29 FOMC decision

`fed-jul26-no-change` — the densest pair in the sample — resolved mid-recording: the statement (no change) dropped at 18:00 UTC (14:00 ET) with the recorder on its normal ~60s cadence. What each venue's book did:

| venue | last two-sided quote before release | first after |
|---|---|---|
| kalshi | 17:57:51 UTC (mid 81.5¢) | never two-sided again |
| polymarket | 17:59:53 UTC (mid 99.4¢) | never two-sided again |

- **Kalshi does not trade the announcement.** Its book was pulled 128s before the release stamp and never returned — the market's scheduled close IS the announcement time. Event-time price discovery on this pair was structurally 100% Polymarket.
- **Polymarket repriced inside one snapshot bracket**: mid 79.9¢ at 17:58:52 → 99.4¢ at 17:59:53 (61s bracket, jump 19.6¢). The landing snapshot is stamped 6s BEFORE the official 18:00:00 release. One recorder, NTP clock, books fetched seconds after the stamp — a few seconds of skew is plausible in either direction, so the defensible claim is: the reprice completed within seconds of the official release, not that anyone traded ahead of it.
- The lock trade dies BEFORE the event, not at it: with Kalshi closed, no new pair position can be opened and none needs to be — a lock holds to resolution by construction. The practical constraint is entry capacity, which ended when Kalshi's book was pulled.

## Caveats

- Both venues are sampled at the same instant per snapshot, so there is no cross-venue clock skew inside a tick — but anything faster than the cadence is invisible (see `simultaneous`).
- Kalshi mids move on a cent grid; Polymarket's finer grid produces more small moves — the threshold sensitivity table bounds how much that asymmetry matters.
- Events are pooled across pairs and days and treated as independent; clustered news moves violate that mildly.
- Sparse-sample study: rates are honest but confidence grows with the recorder (running continuously since 2026-07-21).
- The event study is n=1 by nature: one release, one venue pair, one recorder. The venue-behavior asymmetry (closed vs trading through) is structural and will replicate; the timing bracket may not.
